vaccine.title: The Leicester anti-vaccination march
vaccine.line: Tens of thousands marched in Leicester against compulsory smallpox vaccination, led by men jailed for not vaccinating their children.

vaccine.title: Wakefield’s MMR autism scare
vaccine.line: A Lancet paper by Andrew Wakefield, later retracted, linked the MMR vaccine to autism; UK vaccination rates fell and measles cases rose.

vaccine.title: Northern Nigeria’s polio vaccine boycott
vaccine.line: Kano and other northern Nigerian states halted polio vaccination amid rumors it caused infertility and HIV; polio cases surged and spread abroad.

springtime.title: The revolutions of 1820
springtime.line: A Spanish army revolt forced the king to restore a liberal constitution, and within months revolts broke out in Naples and Portugal.

springtime.title: The anticolonial uprisings of 1919
springtime.line: In spring 1919, mass protests against foreign domination erupted in Egypt, Korea, India and China, all invoking Wilson’s promise of self-determination.

phone.title: The first text message is sent
phone.line: Engineer Neil Papworth sent “Merry Christmas” to a Vodafone director’s phone, the first SMS, and texting went on to reshape daily life.

phone.title: Japan’s i-mode puts the web on phones
phone.line: NTT DoCoMo’s i-mode put email and websites on ordinary phones, drew over 30 million Japanese users by 2002 and popularized emoji.

yellow.title: Bismarck’s edited Ems telegram
yellow.line: Bismarck edited a royal telegram to read like an insult and fed it to the press; French outrage helped spark war.

yellow.title: The AI-faked Pentagon explosion
yellow.line: An apparently AI-generated image of an explosion near the Pentagon spread via verified Twitter accounts, briefly knocking US stock markets lower.

titanic.title: The de Havilland Comet crashes
titanic.line: Britain’s Comet, the first jet airliner and a prestige symbol, was grounded after two broke apart in midair from metal fatigue.

titanic.title: The sinking of the Andrea Doria
titanic.line: Italy’s luxury liner, billed as one of the safest afloat, sank after a collision; its tilt left half its lifeboats unusable.

weimar.title: The Yuan dynasty’s paper money collapse
weimar.line: To fund wars against rebels, China’s Mongol-led Yuan dynasty printed paper money ever faster in the 1350s until it was nearly worthless.

weimar.title: Nationalist China’s gold yuan collapse
weimar.line: Launched in August 1948, Nationalist China’s gold yuan was printed without limit and was nearly worthless within a year, sapping middle-class support.

weimar.title: Yugoslavia’s hyperinflation under sanctions
weimar.line: Printing money to cover deficits amid war and sanctions, Yugoslavia saw prices rise about 313 million percent in January 1994 alone.

dust.title: The mystery haze of 536
dust.line: Volcanic haze dimmed the sun for about 18 months; Procopius said it shone like the moon, and crops failed across Eurasia.

dust.title: The 1997 Southeast Asian haze
dust.line: Land-clearing fires in drought-hit Indonesia smothered Southeast Asia in smoke, often cutting visibility in Sumatra and Borneo below 100 meters.

dust.title: Sydney’s red dust storm
dust.line: Winds lifted topsoil from drought-stricken inland Australia and turned Sydney’s sky red in the biggest dust storm in about 70 years.

transistor.title: Volta builds the first battery
transistor.line: Alessandro Volta stacked zinc and silver discs with brine-soaked cloth to make the first battery, which opened the age of electricity.

transistor.title: The discovery of nuclear fission
transistor.line: In a Berlin lab, Hahn and Strassmann split uranium atoms; within seven years, fission had produced nuclear reactors and atomic bombs.

transistor.title: Maiman builds the first laser
transistor.line: Theodore Maiman built the first laser, jokingly called “a solution looking for a problem”; lasers now carry internet data and scan barcodes.

springs.title: Lois Gibbs and Love Canal
springs.line: Homemaker Lois Gibbs organized neighbors over toxic waste buried under their Niagara Falls neighborhood, forcing evacuations and helping inspire the Superfund law.

springs.title: Chico Mendes defends the Amazon
springs.line: Rubber tapper Chico Mendes fought ranchers clearing the Amazon; his 1988 murder made world headlines and led Brazil to create forest reserves.

volcker.title: Britain doubles rates to 15%
volcker.line: To cool a boom and rising inflation, Nigel Lawson doubled UK interest rates from 7.5% to 15%; a recession followed in 1990.

volcker.title: Russia raises rates to a record 21%
volcker.line: As wartime spending fueled inflation, Russia’s central bank raised its key rate from 7.5% to a record 21% within 16 months.

dolly.title: Ivanov’s human-ape hybrid experiments
dolly.line: Funded by the Soviet government, biologist Ilya Ivanov inseminated chimpanzees in French Guinea with human sperm, trying to create a human-ape hybrid.

dolly.title: The Mexico three-parent baby
dolly.line: A US doctor went to Mexico, where he said “there are no rules,” to make a baby with DNA from three people.

blackout.title: The southern Brazil blackout of 1999
blackout.line: Lightning at one substation triggered a cascade that darkened São Paulo and Rio, affecting an estimated 75 to 97 million Brazilians.

blackout.title: The European blackout of 2006
blackout.line: Switching off a German power line so a cruise ship could pass split Europe’s grid, cutting power to over 15 million customers.

blackout.title: The Argentina and Uruguay blackout
blackout.line: A grid operator’s error set off a 30-second cascade that blacked out nearly all of Argentina and Uruguay, about 48 million people.
